newsitem.title: USA: Harrah's to take Q4 charges totaling $50 mln.
newsitem.headline: Harrah's to take Q4 charges totaling $50 mln.

text.p: Harrah's Entertainment Inc said on Tuesday it would take special charges in fourth quarter 1996 totaling about $50 million pre-tax, which is about $0.27 per share after-tax.
The company said in a statement that as a result, Harrah's expected to report a fourth quarter 1996 net loss per share of about $0.05. The charges relate to several items.
Harrah's will write down the value of its original Tunica, Miss., casino which opened in 1993. The company does not expect to own or operate the facility long-term.

A final decision on how to exit the original Harrah's Tunica casino will be made by mid-year. The company intends to focus its efforts in Tunica on its Harrah's Tunica Mardi Gras Casino which opened in April 1996.
Other charges include reserves for contingent liabilities and the write down of non-operating assets to their realizable value.
In addition, Harrah's will stop managing the two casinos operating under the Harrah's brand name in Central City and Black Hawk, Colo., effective no later than March 31.
